Get started

Source: vignettes/get-started.Rmd
get-started.Rmd
library(tidypptsdm)

tidypptsdm

tidypptsdm watches the feeding stations of a pig performance test from day to day. It answers the questions of the daily round: is every station recording, are the transponders read, does every pig still eat, and how did feed intake and body weight develop over the last days?

The data are read and prepared with tidypptsda: read_station() reads NEDAP or FIRE exports and prep_visits() turns them into one standard visit table (feed intake in g, body weight in kg, duration in seconds, unidentified visits kept with identified = FALSE, pigs moved to another station resolved). Both functions are re-exported, so library(tidypptsdm) is enough.

library(tidypptsdm)

mon <- run_monitor(tidypptsda::nedap, days = 7, verbose = 0)
mon
#> 
#> ── NEDAP monitor: 2024-05-19 to 2024-05-25 ─────────────────────────────────────
#> ℹ 2 stations, 28 pigs; on 2024-05-25: 366 visits, 84.8 kg feed
#> ✔ No alerts
#> Tables: $stations, $houses, $pigs, $pig_summary, $hours, $alerts. Write them
#> with write_monitor_report() or write_monitor_tables().

Internal helpers

Small internal tools shared by every function of the package:

  • verbosity: exported functions have verbose = 0/1/2 (silent / summary / details), as in tidypptsda;
  • input: as_visits() accepts a folder or files, a raw export, the result of read_station() or of prep_visits(), and always returns a copy, so user objects are never modified;
  • window: monitor_window() turns days and end_date into the dates of the monitoring window.

Re-exported from tidypptsda

One monitoring run

run_monitor() is the function for the daily round. It prepares the visits once, computes every table over the last days days and lists the alerts of the last day. Its result goes to write_monitor_report(), write_monitor_tables() and plot_monitor().

The window ends on end_date. By default this is the last day in the data; when that is today, it is the day before, because an export taken during the day has an incomplete last day.

mon <- run_monitor(tidypptsda::nedap, days = 7)
#> 
#> ── Preparing NEDAP visits ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Daily tables

Each table has one row per unit and day of the window, also for days without any visit (counts are then 0). That is what makes a station that stopped recording, or a pig that stopped eating, visible.

Stations

st

Houses

A house is a group of stations, named by the first house_width characters of the station ID.

monitor_houses(tidypptsda::nedap, days = 5, verbose = 0)

Alerts

Wide tables

The daily tables are long: one row per unit and day. wide_table() turns one column into a table with the units in rows and the days (or hours) in columns, as in the Excel workbook.

mon <- run_monitor(tidypptsda::nedap, verbose = 0)
wide_table(mon$stations, "n_visits")
#> Key: <location>
#>    location 05-19 05-20 05-21 05-22 05-23 05-24 05-25 total

Plots

plot_monitor() draws one plot per station. There are five types:

  • "trend": pigs, visits, unidentified visits, occupation time, feed intake and body weight over the window; days without any visit are shaded red;
  • "intake": stacked bars of the feed intake of each pig on each day: its share of the station’s feed (top) and kg (bottom), as fid_monitor() of pptsdm drew them; pigs that did not visit or ate too little on the last day are marked in the legend;
  • "heatmap": feed intake of every pig on every day as a heat map, with a cross for a day without visit and a circle for a low-feed day;
  • "weight": recorded body weights per day as box plots;
  • "hours": visits, occupation time and feed intake per hour of the last day.
mon <- run_monitor(tidypptsda::nedap, verbose = 0)
plot_monitor(mon, "intake")$plot[[1]]

Saving plots 

mon <- run_monitor(tidypptsda::nedap, verbose = 0)
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "monitor_plots")
save_monitor_plots(plot_monitor(mon, "trend"), dir)
#> ✔ Saved 2 of 2 plots to /tmp/RtmpqqKEAm/monitor_plots
unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE)

HTML report

write_monitor_report() writes the monitor as a small offline website, as write_report() does in tidypptsda: an overview page with the alerts and a table of all stations, then one page per station with its plots and its pigs. Turn the pages with the arrow keys and type a pig ID to jump to its station.

mon <- run_monitor(tidypptsda::nedap, verbose = 0)
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "monitor_report")
write_monitor_report(mon, dir)
#> ✔ Report of 2 stations written to /tmp/RtmpqqKEAm/monitor_report/index.html
unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE)

Excel workbook and CSV files 

mon <- run_monitor(tidypptsda::nedap, verbose = 0)
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "monitor_tables")
write_monitor_tables(mon, dir, format = "csv")
#> ✔ Wrote 6 CSV files to /tmp/RtmpqqKEAm/monitor_tables
unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE)

Run every day

schedule_monitor() writes an R script that reads the export folder, runs the monitor and writes the report and the workbook into a folder named after the last day. On Windows the script is registered in the Task Scheduler (with the taskscheduleR package). On Linux and macOS the function prints the line to add with crontab -e.

folder <- file.path(tempdir(), "exports")
dir.create(folder, showWarnings = FALSE)
data.table::fwrite(tidypptsda::nedap, file.path(folder, "nedap.csv"))
out <- file.path(tempdir(), "monitor_runs")
script <- schedule_monitor(folder, out, days = 7, register = FALSE)
#> ✔ Monitor script written to /tmp/RtmpqqKEAm/monitor_runs/tidypptsdm_monitor.R
cat(readLines(script), sep = "\n")
#> # Written by tidypptsdm::schedule_monitor() on 2026-10-31 00:50
#> # Daily monitor of the testing stations: edit the settings below if needed.
#> mon <- tidypptsdm::run_monitor("/tmp/RtmpqqKEAm/exports", days = 7)
#> out <- file.path("/tmp/RtmpqqKEAm/monitor_runs", format(mon$settings$end_date))
#> tidypptsdm::write_monitor_report(mon, out)
#> tidypptsdm::write_monitor_tables(mon, out, format = "xlsx")
unlink(c(folder, out), recursive = TRUE)
